title: AI Risk Management
learning_outcomes: Explain identifying ai-related risks and how it connects to ai risk management.
Apply mapping affected users and stakeholders in the example and predict the output before running it.
Test one realistic edge case for ai risk management and explain what the example does not prove.

content.intro: This lesson covers ai risk management through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Document risk decisions, policy boundaries, stakeholder impact, licensing, applicable law, and governance ownership; legal requirements depend on jurisdiction and use case.
content.why_it_matters: Identifying AI-related risks is a control problem as much as a model-behavior problem. Establish explicit boundaries in trusted application code, minimize data exposure, test realistic misuse and failure cases, and record who is responsible for reviewing residual risk. A prompt alone is not a security boundary.

items.title: Mapping affected users and stakeholders
items.text: Mapping affected users and stakeholders requires a documented decision that fits the use case and jurisdiction. Identify affected stakeholders, distinguish binding obligations from voluntary guidance, retain evidence for the decision, and revisit the conclusion when the model, data, product, or applicable rules change.

items.title: Selecting and implementing mitigations
items.text: Use selecting and implementing mitigations as a lens for understanding ai risk management. Trace its inputs, the operation or decision it describes, the result a learner can observe, and the limitations that matter for the intended task. Confirm the idea with a small example and an explicit check rather than relying on fluent or plausible output.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice identifying ai-related risks within ai risk management: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.

summary: AI Risk Management is one part of a larger generative AI application lifecycle.
Use explicit inputs, criteria, and reproducible examples to test the concept.
Document uncertainty, failure modes, security considerations, and version assumptions.
